name: Koongo
summary: Shopify app that syncs product feeds, stock and orders across Amazon, eBay, Bol, Zalando, Allegro and 500-plus channels from one dashboard.
best_for: Shopify merchants selling across several European marketplaces (Bol, Zalando, Allegro, Cdiscount, Miinto and the rest) who need inventory and order sync to run automatically, and who have priced their own item, feed and order counts against the surcharge table rather than the headline
skip_if: you sell on one channel or need product feeds only, where the feed-manager-only form from $14.50 or a dedicated feed app is cheaper; or your catalogue and order volume sit far enough above the included limits that the surcharges, not the plan, become the price
honest_knock:
The headline price is a base, not a bill. Each paid plan includes 1,000 items, 5 feeds, one marketplace wizard and 100 orders a month, and the listing says plainly that surcharges apply for extras used across all four of those dimensions. For a store with a real catalogue selling on several European marketplaces, every one of those limits is one you pass in week one. Price your own numbers on koongo.com's surcharge table before you take $39 seriously.

The two pricing pages also do not quote the same bill. The App Store lists $39, $79 and $119 and bills in USD. koongo.com lists €35, €69 and €99 and states that all prices exclude VAT. Depending on where you trade and how you are registered, those are meaningfully different amounts for the same plan, and nothing on either page reconciles them.

Then the record, which is the most useful thing on this listing. 4.4 from 98 reviews is the lowest average in this category among the apps Shopify shows beside it, and the breakdown explains why: 84 five-star ratings sit alongside six one-star ones. The critical reviews are specific rather than vague, which makes them worth reading in full. In July 2026 a Belgian merchant described a repricer set to Monitoring Mode that still blocked updates to live Bol offers because of MinimumPrice errors, so a delivery-promise change never reached the marketplace. In January 2026 a UK merchant described unresolved integration errors on OnBuy and a refused refund, with Koongo replying publicly that they had reached out several times without response. Neither is disqualifying on its own. Together they describe an app whose complexity is real and whose marketplace integrations sometimes need support to untangle, which is consistent with the vendor's own listing offering personal onboarding for complex setups.

One more line to read before you install: the listing states the app views sensitive customer data as well as device and activity data, and can view and edit products, orders and custom data. Marketplace order sync needs customer details to work, so that is expected, but it makes this a processor of personal data on your behalf rather than a feed formatter.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Lite Plan · per month on the App Store listing for 1,000 items, 5 feeds, one marketplace wizard and 100 orders a month, with surcharges for every extra item, feed, marketplace and order
pricing.notes: (read 2026-08-23 on apps.shopify.com/koongo, listed as “Koongo: Sell on Marketplaces”, and on koongo.com/pricing) Four tiers on the listing, separated by update frequency rather than by capability. Free covers one store language, 100 items or SKUs, 5 product feeds, one marketplace wizard and up to 10 orders a month, updating once a day. Lite is $39 a month and updates every 6 hours, Starter is $79 and updates every 30 minutes, and Pro is $119 and updates every 15 minutes. All three include 1,000 items, 5 feeds, one marketplace wizard (in August 2026 a second came free on a summer promotion; the listing no longer shows it on 10 October 2026), and 100 orders a month. All three also carry a 7-day free trial. Every paid tier states surcharges for extras used — items, feeds, marketplaces and orders — and each is also sold in a feed-manager-only form, from $14.50 for Lite, $29 for Starter and $41 for Pro. All charges on the listing are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. The vendor's own pricing page sells the same four plans in euros at €0, €35, €69 and €99 a month, and states that all prices exclude VAT. Each plan is broken into Core, Marketplace Manager, Feed Manager and Ads Manager modules with separate prices. There is also a surcharge table for extra stores, items, orders, marketplaces, feeds and team seats, where an extra 100 orders runs from €10.00 down to €2.00 as volume grows. Developer Koongo, a product of NoStress Commerce s.r.o., Prague; the app launched on 5 November 2014 and had 98 reviews at the time of writing. Re-read 10 October 2026: the App Store prices ($39, $79, $119) and koongo.com prices (€35, €69, €99 excluding VAT) are unchanged, and koongo.com's surcharge table now prints the amounts per plan: an extra 100 orders at €10.00 down to €2.00 on every paid plan, an extra 1,000 items at €1.00 down to €0.50 on Lite, €2.00 down to €1.00 on Starter and €2.80 down to €1.40 on Pro, and an extra marketplace at €15.00, €30.00 or €42.00. Re-read 20 November 2026 on the App Store listing: Free, Lite $39, Starter $79 and Pro $119 a month are unchanged, as are the feed-manager-only prices from $14.50, $29 and $41 and the 7-day trial. koongo.com/pricing now loads its plan table only in the browser, so the euro amounts were not re-read that day; its FAQ, read the same day, names a fourth paid plan, Ultimate, with updates every 5 minutes, email, live chat and video-call support, 60 minutes of personal assistance a month and four included add-ons, suited to around 300+ orders a day, and says all prices exclude VAT.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Koongo on a Shopify development store: the install (the vendor account was created automatically), a Google Shopping XML feed built in 4 clicks and about 2 minutes with 18 items exported, the Free Plan limits, the four plans (Lite 14.50, Starter 29.00, Pro 41.00 and Ultimate 58.00 dollars a month, each Starting on) and the Lite summary of 14.50 dollars. The feed address answered with a 200 without any login, and 16 of the 18 items had an empty g:id field. A privacy window with a pre-ticked newsletter box appeared at the start and was not accepted; it was hidden only for the screenshots. The Shopify approval screen was not reached, no trial was started and nothing was paid. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the App Store page was opened at 16:59 (admin and vendor app set to English by us), the install form was submitted, the dialog Install app asked for View customer data (sensitive data, device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (store owner) and View and edit store data (products, orders, custom data, other data), and Install was clicked at about 17:01. The vendor app opened on its own site in Dutch (Installatie bezig, then App is succesvol geinstalleerd and U bent op het Free abonnement); no separate account or password was asked, because the account was created automatically from the Shopify store. The cookie banner was declined. We switched the language of the app to EN. Privacy window: at the start in the app a window appeared with the title Your privacy is important to us, links to the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use and Terms and Conditions, a pre-ticked newsletter sign-up and an Accept button. It was NOT accepted, because accepting terms is outside the permission of the tester; the feed and the preview were already visible behind it. For the screenshots the window was hidden in our own tab with display none, so the screenshots show the app without that window. Hiding it is not an acceptance, and the real first screen includes the window. Core action, a product feed for Google Shopping: after the install this took 4 clicks (choose the channel Google Shopping, the type Product - USA, Canada, the format XML, and Add channel profile) and about 2 minutes (about 17:03). The result was the page Feed Preview for Google shopping (#1) with Exported 18, NOT SUBMITTED YET and the banner that Category Mapping is not complete. The feed has a public address on the vendor domain; fetching it without a login gave HTTP 200 and 16258 bytes. The XML held 18 items. In 16 of the 18 items the g:id field was empty (only two items, with ids like sku-hosted-1 and sku-managed-1, had one), the g:description field was empty in most items and identifier_exists was FALSE. This is a store with a handful of test products, so the empty fields may come from how the test store was filled, and we did not check the cause. No Google Merchant Center or marketplace account was connected and nothing was submitted. Plans: Shopify managed pricing does not exist for this app (Select a plan said to contact the app developer for help choosing a plan); the plans are on the vendor site under My Plan and Pricing. The Free Plan since 17 Nov 2026 lists Stores 1, Products 100, Feeds 1, Marketplaces 1, Ads 1 and Orders 10/month, with orders, products and product status synced every 24 hours. Choose Plan (Get started with a 7-day free trial) shows four plans Starting on: Lite 14.50$ a month (updates every 6 hours), Starter 29.00$ (every 30 minutes), Pro 41.00$ (every 15 minutes) and Ultimate 58.00$ (every 5 minutes; email, chat and video-call help). Modules and Add-ons list Feeds (5 feeds included, extra 5 feeds for 6$ a month), Marketplaces (1 marketplace included, extra 1 marketplace for 18$ a month; the module showed 24.50$ a month) and Ads (extra 1 advertising channel for 10$ a month; 9.50$ a month). Differences with the dossier: the dossier gives Lite $39, Starter $79 and Pro $119 a month on the App Store listing and EUR 35, 69 and 99 on the vendor site, and says each is also sold in a feed-manager-only form from $14.50, $29 and $41; the app showed Starting on 14.50$, 29.00$ and 41.00$, which equal those feed-manager-only prices, plus a fourth plan, Ultimate at 58.00$, that the dossier does not have, and no $39, $79 or $119 plan was shown, so the app tiers and the dossier tiers do not line up. The dossier says the Free plan has 5 product feeds; the Free Plan page of the app says Feeds 1. Products 100, one marketplace, 10 orders a month and the daily update match. Checkout: NOT reached. On the Summary tab for Lite the vendor showed Fixed Monthly Fee 14.50$, Estimated Usage Fees 0.00$ and TOTAL 14.50$ with a tick box for the Terms and Conditions, Data Privacy Policy and Usage Charges Policy and the button Start My 7 Days Free Trial. Agreeing to the terms and starting the trial was not done, so the Shopify screen Approve subscription was never opened and no price, tax or renewal term at the end of the buying path was observed. Cancelling: no subscription was started, so nothing could be cancelled; the banner says Cancel anytime. The way to stop was to uninstall the app. Not tested: linking a marketplace (Bol, Amazon), stock and order sync, category mapping, the Merchant Center connection, any paid plan and the trial, and the pain around a setting that blocks updates (that needs a marketplace account). No theme change was made. Clean up: the app was uninstalled through Settings, Apps in our own tab and our own tabs were closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. Name, e-mail and initials in the sidebar of the vendor app were cleared in the page by the tester before the screenshots; we checked that nothing is left in the images, and the store name is hidden in the images. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: A privacy window with a pre-ticked newsletter box covers the start, the feed was made with 16 of 18 empty g:id fields and a public address without login, category mapping was not complete, the app showed four plans Starting on 14.50, 29.00, 41.00 and 58.00 dollars where the dossier has Lite $39, Starter $79 and Pro $119, and the Free Plan page says Feeds 1 where the dossier says 5 product feeds.

The cookie banner was declined. We switched the language of the app to EN. Privacy window: at the start in the app a window appeared with the title Your privacy is important to us, links to the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use and Terms and Conditions, a pre-ticked newsletter sign-up and an Accept button. It was NOT accepted, because accepting terms is outside the permission of the tester; the feed and the preview were already visible behind it. For the screenshots the window was hidden in our own tab with display none, so the screenshots show the app without that window. Hiding it is not an acceptance, and the real first screen includes the window. Core action, a product feed for Google Shopping: after the install this took 4 clicks (choose the channel Google Shopping, the type Product - USA, Canada, the format XML, and Add channel profile) and about 2 minutes (about 17:03). The result was the page Feed Preview for Google shopping (#1) with Exported 18, NOT SUBMITTED YET and the banner that Category Mapping is not complete. The feed has a public address on the vendor domain; fetching it without a login gave HTTP 200 and 16258 bytes. The XML held 18 items. In 16 of the 18 items the g:id field was empty (only two items, with ids like sku-hosted-1 and sku-managed-1, had one), the g:description field was empty in most items and identifier_exists was FALSE. This is a store with a handful of test products, so the empty fields may come from how the test store was filled, and we did not check the cause. No Google Merchant Center or marketplace account was connected and nothing was submitted. Plans: Shopify managed pricing does not exist for this app (Select a plan said to contact the app developer for help choosing a plan); the plans are on the vendor site under My Plan and Pricing. The Free Plan since 17 Nov 2026 lists Stores 1, Products 100, Feeds 1, Marketplaces 1, Ads 1 and Orders 10/month, with orders, products and product status synced every 24 hours. Choose Plan (Get started with a 7-day free trial) shows four plans Starting on: Lite 14.50$ a month (updates every 6 hours), Starter 29.00$ (every 30 minutes), Pro 41.00$ (every 15 minutes) and Ultimate 58.00$ (every 5 minutes; email, chat and video-call help). Modules and Add-ons list Feeds (5 feeds included, extra 5 feeds for 6$ a month), Marketplaces (1 marketplace included, extra 1 marketplace for 18$ a month; the module showed 24.50$ a month) and Ads (extra 1 advertising channel for 10$ a month; 9.50$ a month). Differences with the dossier: the dossier gives Lite $39, Starter $79 and Pro $119 a month on the App Store listing and EUR 35, 69 and 99 on the vendor site, and says each is also sold in a feed-manager-only form from $14.50, $29 and $41; the app showed Starting on 14.50$, 29.00$ and 41.00$, which equal those feed-manager-only prices, plus a fourth plan, Ultimate at 58.00$, that the dossier does not have, and no $39, $79 or $119 plan was shown, so the app tiers and the dossier tiers do not line up. The dossier says the Free plan has 5 product feeds; the Free Plan page of the app says Feeds 1. Products 100, one marketplace, 10 orders a month and the daily update match. Checkout: NOT reached. On the Summary tab for Lite the vendor showed Fixed Monthly Fee 14.50$, Estimated Usage Fees 0.00$ and TOTAL 14.50$ with a tick box for the Terms and Conditions, Data Privacy Policy and Usage Charges Policy and the button Start My 7 Days Free Trial. Agreeing to the terms and starting the trial was not done, so the Shopify screen Approve subscription was never opened and no price, tax or renewal term at the end of the buying path was observed. Cancelling: no subscription was started, so nothing could be cancelled; the banner says Cancel anytime. No theme change was made. Clean up: the app was uninstalled through Settings, Apps in our own tab and our own tabs were closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. Name, e-mail and initials in the sidebar of the vendor app were cleared in the page by the tester before the screenshots; we checked that nothing is left in the images, and the store name is hidden in the images. No kit records were entered. A check of this export route with synthetic records, on the account and date stated. Re-importing the export was not tested. The exported file was not opened, so what it contains is unverified. Friction is described, not scored; this is not a verdict on the product.
